statement: What is the area of the triangle whose vertices are $(1, 2)$, $(7, 4)$ and $(3, 8)$?

choices.misconception: I used the horizontal width of the triangle, 6, as the base and its vertical height, 6, as the height, as if the triangle had a horizontal side, and got (1/2)(6)(6) = 18.
I drew the 6 by 6 box around the triangle but subtracted only the two corner triangles of area 6, missing the one with legs 4 and 4, so I got 36 - 12 = 24.
I used the shoelace sum correctly but forgot to divide it by 2, getting 32.
I gave the area of the 6 by 6 box around the triangle and forgot to cut off the three corner triangles.

hints: Draw the smallest rectangle with horizontal and vertical sides that contains the triangle.
The box runs from $x = 1$ to $x = 7$ and from $y = 2$ to $y = 8$. The parts of the box outside the triangle are three right triangles.
The three outside right triangles have legs $6$ and $2$, $4$ and $4$, and $2$ and $6$, so their areas are $6$, $8$ and $6$. Subtract them from $36$.

solutions.reliable: Enclose the triangle in the box $1 \le x \le 7$, $2 \le y \le 8$, which has area $36$. Outside the triangle but inside the box are three right triangles: below the side from $(1, 2)$ to $(7, 4)$, with legs $6$ and $2$ and area $6$; to the right of the side from $(7, 4)$ to $(3, 8)$, with legs $4$ and $4$ and area $8$; and to the left of the side from $(3, 8)$ to $(1, 2)$, with legs $2$ and $6$ and area $6$. The triangle's area is $36 - 6 - 8 - 6 = 16$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
